title: Look at the camel. How was it made?
subtitle: The animal their whole life depended on

row.title: an amazing creation
sub: look at how it was made

then: The people of Makkah were {trap}ignoring the message carelessly.{/trap} So the surah points at the camel, their most common animal. Ibn Kathir: {idea}extremely strong, yet gentle, led by a weak rider{/idea}, and giving milk, meat and hair.
now: Your phone, your cat on the sofa, your own hand. You use them so often you stopped seeing them. {idea}The verse asks you to look again at the most ordinary thing in your day.{/idea}
old: Everyday things are boring. Signs must be something dramatic.
new: The most ordinary thing in my life is a sign if I look.
try: Pick one animal or object you see daily and spend one minute noticing how it is made.

title: And the sky: how was it raised?
subtitle: The roof over every journey
then: The judge Shurayh used to say: {idea}come out with us to look at the camels and how they were created, and at the sky and how it was raised.{/idea} Ibn Kathir links it to the verse: have they not looked at the heaven above them, how We built it?
now: You check the sky only on a weather app. Head down on the commute, eyes on the screen. {idea}The sky has been held up over you your whole life{/idea} and you have barely looked at it this week.
old: The sky is just there. It does not say anything to me.
new: The raised sky is a daily sign of the One who raised it.
try: Step outside today, look up for one full minute, and say SubhanAllah.

title: And the mountains: how were they set firm?
subtitle: Mountains planted so the earth stays steady
then: Ibn Kathir: {idea}they are firmly fixed so that the earth does not sway with its dwellers{/idea}, and He made them with benefits and minerals. The traveler in Arabia always had a mountain in front of him. The verse asks him to think about who put it there.
now: The ground under your house is still while you sleep. You never think about it until the news shows an earthquake somewhere. {idea}Your steadiness was arranged long before you needed it.{/idea}
old: Stability in my life is mostly my own doing.
new: Even the ground I stand on was made steady for me.
try: When you feel shaken today, place your feet flat on the floor and remember who keeps it still.

title: And the earth: how was it spread out?
subtitle: Four things the traveler sees, one Maker

row.title: He made it, so He is my Lord

then: Ibn Kathir: {idea}He directs the bedouin to consider what he himself witnesses{/idea}: the camel he rides, the sky above, the mountain ahead, the earth beneath. A bedouin named Dimam later swore by these same things when he asked the Prophet ﷺ if Allah had sent him.
now: Your morning walk to the bus stop. Pavement under you, sky above, a hill or a skyline ahead. {idea}Four signs on the most boring route of your day.{/idea} They all ask the same question: who made this, and do you live like you know?
old: I believe Allah made everything, but it does not change my day.
new: If He made all I see, He is the One I should be living for.
try: On your next walk, name the four things this passage mentions and say who made them.

title: So remind. Reminding is your whole job.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ is told his role is to remind
then: After the signs, the instruction: {idea}remind the people with what you have been sent with.{/idea} Ibn Kathir links it to the verse: {idea}your duty is only to convey, and on Us is the reckoning.{/idea}
now: You keep telling your brother to pray and he keeps not praying. You start to feel you have failed. {idea}Your job was to remind, kindly and clearly.{/idea} The rest is not in your hands.
old: If they do not change, my reminding was a failure.
new: My part is the reminder. The result belongs to Allah.
try: Make dua for someone you have been trying to remind, and let go of the outcome.

title: You are not their controller.
subtitle: No one can force faith into a heart
then: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: {idea}you are not a dictator over them.{/idea} Ibn Kathir: {trap}you cannot create faith in their hearts.{/trap} Ibn Zayd said: you are not the one who can force them to believe.
now: The nagging messages. The pressure at family gatherings. Turning a teenager's every mistake into a sermon. {trap}Control often pushes people further away.{/trap} {idea}Faith is placed in a heart by Allah, not by force.{/idea}
old: If I push hard enough, I can make them believe.
new: I cannot control a heart. I can only remind and pray.
try: Replace one lecture you planned to give someone this week with one kind act toward them.

title: But the one who turns his back and rejects.
subtitle: Turning away from the truth by heart and tongue
then: Ibn Kathir: {trap}he turns away from acting on its pillars, and disbelieves in the truth with his heart and his tongue.{/trap} He compares it to the verse: he neither believed nor prayed, but denied and turned away.
now: It rarely starts with a big rejection. You skip, then you avoid, then you argue against what you skipped. {idea}Turning away is a direction, and you can notice it early in yourself.{/idea}
old: Turning away is something other people do.
new: I check which part of the truth I am quietly turning my back on.
try: Name one thing you know is right but have been avoiding, and take one step toward it.

title: Allah Himself will deal with him.
subtitle: The greatest punishment, decided by Allah alone
then: The verse is plain: {trap}Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment.{/trap} Coming right after you are not their controller, it puts the judgement where it belongs: {idea}with Allah, not with the one reminding.{/idea}
now: It is easy to sit in judgement of people online, deciding who is doomed. {idea}The verse takes that seat away from you.{/idea} Judgement is Allah's. Your own record is the one you can still work on.
old: I can tell who is going to be punished.
new: Punishment is Allah's to decide. My task is my own record.
try: When you catch yourself judging someone today, turn the thought into a dua for both of you.

title: Every one of them is coming back to Us.
subtitle: The return is to Allah, without exception

row.title: a return
sub: back to the One who sent you

then: Ibn Kathir: {idea}their place of return and their resort.{/idea} The surah opened by asking about the Overwhelming Day. Near its close it says plainly where everyone is heading.
now: Boarding pass, return flight. You always check the return date. {idea}Your life has a return date too{/idea}, and the One you return to is the One who made the camel, the sky, and you.
old: Life goes on and then it just stops.
new: Life is a journey that ends in a return to Allah.
try: Say Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un once today, slowly, about your own life.

title: And then it is on Us to take their account.
subtitle: Every deed reckoned and repaid fairly
then: Ibn Kathir: {idea}We will reckon their deeds and requite them.{/idea} {reward}If they did good, they will receive good{/reward}, and if evil, evil. The surah ends here, the account placed with Allah, as it told the Prophet ﷺ in verse 21.
now: The extra shift no one thanked you for. The patience with a difficult parent. The charity you never mentioned. {reward}The account is kept by Allah, and nothing good is dropped.{/reward}
old: Most of what I do goes unnoticed and unrewarded.
new: Every deed is counted by Allah, and good is met with good.
try: Tonight, list three things you did today that you would want in your account.
